title: Moon base: the 354-hour night (option B: NASA's own moving footage, one AI-moved shot)
note: Nov 23. Same sentences and voice; the line 'No base with people has yet run through a lunar night' now comes before the sunlight lines, so the peak starts at 57% of the running time (rule: 50-70%). Shots 1-7 are NASA's own 4K animation (tagged 'Animation' by NASA, no partner's name), from nasa.gov and images.nasa.gov, credit NASA: the monthly videos 'NASA Moon Base: Lunar Landers' (Aug 2026) and 'NASA Moon Base: Rovers and Lunar Terrain Vehicles' (Oct 2026), and the concept animation 'Living and Working on the Moon' (May 2026). Each is a 9:16 window of the 3840x2160 frame, never enlarged; 30 frames a second are played one by one at 24, so nothing judders (motion runs at 80% speed). Shot 8 is AI-moved: first frame a 1088x1920 window of NASA's 4K rendering 'Moon Base Phase 1' (May 2026), motion by the open model LTX-2.3 at 24 frames a second.

shots.job: This shot shows two astronauts at work at a base, a rover behind them and Earth on the horizon, so the viewer sees at once whose night this is. (Landers video, 9:50)
This shot shows an astronaut's glove holding a rock in the dark, lit only by helmet lamps, so the viewer feels what a night there means. (Rovers video, 0:26)
This shot shows a small lander sitting dark and still on the surface, so the viewer sees what 'shutting down' looks like. (Landers video, 9:30)
This shot shows an astronaut kneeling at work beside a rover, so the viewer sees the people a base cannot switch off. (Rovers video, 0:18)
This shot shows an astronaut climbing down a lander's ladder, so the viewer sees an arrival that has not happened yet. (Rovers video, 0:22)
This shot shows a base on a sunlit plain below a ridge near the south pole, long shadows from a low Sun, so the viewer sees the sunlight the line speaks of. (Concept animation, 0:05)
This shot shows the same kind of ground in darkness, with only the base's lamps lit, so the viewer sees it go dark. (Rovers video, 0:06)
This shot shows two astronauts walking to their rover with Earth above the ridge, so the viewer sees what has been promised. (AI-moved from NASA's rendering)

lines.say: A Moon base would face nights about three hundred and fifty-four hours long.
